title: Resolving Ambivalence in Marshallese Navigation: Relearning, Reinterpreting, and Reviving the “Stick Chart” Wave Models
version: Structure and Dynamics 9(1), pp. 8–40; DOI 10.5070/SD991031888. Publisher-rendered English original.
lineage: Firsthand ethnography and participant observation, with instruction and model explanations attributed to Marshallese experts. This revisits the research collaboration reported in Genz et al. (2009) and the Genz interview published by WAM (2014). The publisher's browser-rendered original was readable; direct download presented a challenge page. Attributed review notes retained.

passages.locator: pp. 12–15, Introduction and Marshallese Wave Piloting
passages.note: Distinguishes training at the Rongelap reef, land-based instructional models used with elders, and wave piloting at sea; documents objectives of the Marshallese-led revival.

passages.locator: pp. 29–32, The Stern Test of Landfall and fig. 7
passages.quote: weaving the meto through his sitting mat
passages.note: Identifies Bokin's instruction at Ujae, Joel's recollection of both Bokin's and Eknilang's teachings, and selective use of their models on the return leg. Outbound weather limited wave piloting.
Discusses differences among models and limits of explanations for those differences; effects of displacement and surviving knowledge.
